chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid and al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Abd al-A'la, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man who divorces his wife three times. He said, 'If he is one who treats divorce lightly, it is binding upon him as such.'

key_terms.مُسْتَخِفًّا: one who treats lightly / is casual

ai.seo_question: Is triple divorce final or revocable in Shia fiqh if done in one sitting?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the status of triple divorce (طَلَاق ثَلَاث) in Shia fiqh, distinguishing it from the Sunni view by linking its finality to the husband's intent. The term 'mistaking' or 'treating lightly' (مُسْتَخِفًّا) indicates that if the husband divorces three times in one sitting with the intention of finality, it becomes irrevocable, whereas if done casually without such intent, it may remain revocable. This highlights the Shia emphasis on intention (نية) and context in determining legal outcomes, a key principle in Usul al-Fiqh.
